name: Webster Creek (Mud Lake Wildlife Refuge)
summary: Mud Lake Wildlife Refuge fire tower, built 1939 by USFWS; county survey ties it to a refuge HQ tower that the FFLOS index marks gone; sources disagree.
design: Wood tower with enclosed crow's nest, 110 ft (1941 survey notes); another note in the same survey says about 100 ft and wood, and that other records report a 100 ft steel tower
status_note: Original Mud Lake site: tower gone per FFLOS index. County survey points to the present refuge headquarters tower as the successor; the index marks that HQ tower gone; sources disagree
agency: United States Fish & Wildlife Service (county survey)

access.note: County survey says the HQ tower is standing and open to the public. A refuge brochure labelled 2000 says use is permitted in snow-free months during office hours, with a key from the office. No newer access source read.

events.note: Refuge established as the Mud Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge (Wikipedia)
County survey gives 1939 as the build year for the Mud Lake Wildlife Refuge tower; a note in the Agassiz entry gives 1938
1941 survey notes describe a wood tower with an enclosed crow's nest, 110 ft
Refuge brochure labelled 2000 describes a 100-foot observation tower, usable in snow-free months during office hours with a key from the office
County survey: the refuge headquarters tower reopened in 2005
